newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firm, traders expect more gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firm, traders expect more gains.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended higher, and traders now expect further gains toward next July resistance between 1,060 and 1,065 stg per tonne.
May closed up six at 1,024 and July rose five to 1,043. Total volume stood at 8,130 contracts, with July grabbing 2,073 lots. May 1998 followed with 1,704 lots and July 1998 with 1,471.

Trade buying in the nearbys helped lift July through initial resistance on a triangle formation near 1,040 in the morning. Some traders noted particular interest from a large, privately-held U.S. firm.
Technical buying then emerged near 1,040 stg to push July through next resistance at 1,046, last week's high, to help the contract preserve its upward momentum, traders said.
July reached a high of 1,049 before trimming its gains in the afternoon when New York gapped higher and then stalled.
Nevertheless, traders were bullish on cocoa in the medium term. They said technicals were starting to look more encouraging.
Fundamentally, cocoa was underpinned by underlying concerns that Ivorian shippers were having diffculty fulfilling committments.

Cash cocoa buyers were said to be sidelined this week with scattered purchases from north European industry, but physical traders said Ivorian supply was restricted and there were few offers in the market.
Earlier, exporters and crop analysts in Abidjan said Ivorian exporters with insufficient cocoa stocks to meet April and May contracts were facing a shortage of good quality export grade port arrivals
Sterling's recent weakness against the dollar also helped buoy cocoa, some traders said.
In options, no contracts changed hands.
